findings.claim: The plan's Intent ("the change does not re-register the job") and row r2's behavior text ("does not re-register") are false. Changing detach made the provider call Register again. Nomad recorded job version 19 with an empty diff against 18, opened a new deployment, and updated allocation 3e1235b1 in place without a restart. r2's fails_when (jobspec changes or job replaced) still holds, so the code needs nothing. Only the wording needs fixing, to "re-registers an identical spec; the running allocation is updated in place, not restarted".

verdict.text: The code change is right and small.
`nomad_job.bifrost` now sets `detach = false`, which matches `nomad_job.openviking`.
The new test pins the setting inside the bifrost block.
Gates are green.
The one finding is wording: the plan and r2 claim the change does not re-register the job, and the live evidence shows it did, harmlessly.
Fix the wording, not the code.

Gates, re-run by me with `loopctl gate stamp` from the worktree: `pass gate pre_commit`, `pass gate cli_tests`, `pass eval-row r1`, `stamp green: bb408f2c2a7b424ffbaa9e2d7fea3e1e8df7730fb31acb7866ddf0d78888a1e5`.
Correctness: `null_resource.bifrost_ready` depends on `nomad_job.bifrost` and is replaced when the jobspec hash changes.
With `detach = false`, a jobspec change now blocks the apply until the Nomad deployment succeeds.
Bifrost is a service job with a check and static port 8080 on host networking, count 1.
So the old allocation has stopped and the new one is healthy before the gate polls `/health`.
That closes P1.
When only `detach` changes, the jobspec hash stays the same, so the gate is not replaced and does not re-poll, which is correct.
r1: `test_bifrost_job_waits_for_its_deployment` takes only the `resource "nomad_job" "bifrost"` block, up to its closing brace at column 0, and needs an uncommented `detach = false` line inside it.
Removing the line, setting it to true, or commenting it out all fail the test.
It asserts the row's fails_when.
r2 (judgment): I read the evidence in the briefing and checked the cluster read-only.
`nomad job history bifrost` shows version 19 submitted at 14:27:39 and stable.
`nomad job history -p -version 19` shows no diff against 18.
The latest deployment 2c950259 succeeded.
Allocation 3e1235b1 runs at version 19, and the 2.6/2.7 allocation b6471d9b stopped earlier.
The jobspec did not change and the job was not replaced, so r2's fails_when is not met and the row passes.
Its behavior text and the plan's Intent overstate the result (f1).
Consistency: the new code comment is true and matches the openviking comment.
The comment only says why `detach = false` is set, and makes no claim about re-registration.
No doc under `docs/` or `.okf/` mentions `detach`.
No checklist lines were printed for this round.
f1 (docs, not blocking): plan Intent line 29-30 and the r2 behavior say the change "does not re-register" the job.
It does: the provider's Update calls Register, and Nomad bumps the version even when the spec is identical.
The fix is to say what happened: an identical spec was re-registered, a new deployment ran, and the allocation was updated in place with no restart.
I left `eval_row` unset on purpose.
r2's fails_when is correct and passed, and setting it would block the ticket for the operator over wording.
The plan reviewer's r1 verdict repeats the same claim.
It is a historical record, so leave it alone.
The version bump has a small side effect worth knowing.
Every future change to a provider-only argument on any `nomad_job` (detach, purge_on_destroy, and so on) will add a Nomad job version and run a deployment.
It will not restart allocations when the spec is the same.
